name: Jellyfin Federation
overview: Allows jellyfin servers to federate with each other
description: This Jellyfin plugin allows multiple Jellyfin servers to federate, sharing media libraries in real-time without syncing or copying files. Media can be streamed from one server to another with live transcoding if necessary.

versions.changelog: Robustness pass on the WAN bandwidth checks added in 0.0.32-0.0.35, prompted by a request to make federation resilient behind things like a Cloudflare Tunnel or any other reverse proxy in front of a remote server. Found a real gap: the bandwidth probe and same-network DNS check had no timeout of their own, inheriting the shared HTTP client's 5-minute timeout - meaning a slow or briefly unresponsive remote (tunnel cold-starting, proxy hiccup, etc.) could stall not just its own check but the entire sync cycle for up to 5 minutes, since this runs at the start of every sync. Both now fail fast on their own short, explicit timeouts (20s for the bandwidth probe, 8s for DNS) instead. Also parallelized these checks across servers - previously sequential, so a mapping with several remote servers multiplied any per-server delay by however many needed rechecking that cycle. None of this changes what topology is supported: the adaptive cap was already transport-agnostic, since it measures real achieved throughput against whatever URL is configured rather than assuming anything about network layout - a tunneled or proxied server already gets classified as not-same-network and measured the same as any other internet-only link. No forced item recreation; existing watch progress and ids are untouched.

Tunes the adaptive WAN bitrate cap added in 0.0.32-0.0.34, per feedback that streaming still wasn't fast/high-bitrate enough: (1) the minimum bitrate the auto-cap will ever request is raised from 4 to 10 Mbps - a connection measuring below that still gets 10 Mbps requested rather than something proportionally lower. (2) The safety margin applied to measured bandwidth is raised from 75% to 85% of what a connection actually measures, so less real, usable bandwidth is left unused. (3) The bandwidth measurement itself now samples 5MB instead of 2MB, reducing how much TCP slow-start (the connection ramping up over its first several round-trips) skews a short sample toward reading lower than the connection's real sustained throughput - most noticeable on faster links. No forced item recreation; existing watch progress and ids are untouched.

Continues 0.0.33's WAN-cap staleness fixes and delete-server cleanup with a redesigned config page. Remote user selection is now a dropdown of the remote server's real accounts (name, admin badge) instead of a blind-pasted GUID, fetched on Test/on demand/once per session for already-connected servers, with a manual-entry fallback if a remote can't be reached. Fixed a real bug in the process: per-field autosave silently swallowed errors, so a failed save gave zero feedback - failures now always surface, successes get a brief 'Saved' confirmation. Per-server connection details now default to open instead of hiding Enabled/User/API key behind a collapsed section, with only the genuinely advanced dials (WAN bitrate cap, image API key) moved into a nested, still-collapsed 'Streaming tuning' section. Also fixed a latent gap where adding a new server didn't send its WAN-cap fields at all (harmless today since they'd just take their defaults, but the same missing-field pattern this plugin has been bitten by before).

Builds on 0.0.31's dedup/badge/resume work with a new adaptive WAN bitrate cap for Direct mode, plus two real bugs found while testing it - still no forced item recreation (existing watch progress and ids are untouched). (1) Direct mode previously always pulled the source's raw, untranscoded file straight from the remote - fine on a local network, but when two servers are only connected over the internet, a 25+ Mbps 4K HDR release can exceed the remote's own upload bandwidth and stutter no matter how fast either machine is. A background check now classifies each server as same-network or internet-only and, only for a confirmed internet link, measures what it can actually sustain (via the remote's own bandwidth-test endpoint, the same mechanism jellyfin-web itself uses) and caps to the largest bitrate that fits - direct play otherwise, always, including the entire time before that first check completes. (2) Found on first real test: item.Path was stamped once, at item-creation time, with whatever that check happened to decide right then - but reconciliation never revisits an existing item, so the decision froze forever even after later classification or a fresh measurement changed what it should now be, so it 'worked for some files, not others' depending purely on when each item was created. A static Path is now only ever stamped when it provably cannot go stale (capping off entirely, or a server positively confirmed same-network) - everything else resolves fresh on every playback request instead. (3) A related bug in that same live path reported the original source's real container/codecs even when actually serving a capped transcode; fixed to report what's actually served. (4) Removing a remote server now cleans up immediately - its items are reconciled out of the library right away instead of lingering until the next sync, and its cached network data is dropped instead of leaking in memory.

0.0.30 stopped new federated items from being created with IsShortcut/ShortcutPath set (which broke playback - see 0.0.30's changelog), but reconciliation only ever creates and deletes items, never updates them in place, so every item already persisted under 0.0.26-0.0.29 kept the stale IsShortcut=true and kept crashing on every playback attempt exactly as before - confirmed directly in a user-supplied log taken after upgrading to 0.0.30. This release adds the missing one-time migration: every existing federated item is rebuilt once more so the stale flag is actually cleared. Local watch progress on federated items is reset, as with prior rebuilds.

Fixes federated movies/episodes getting stuck loading (or silently failing to play at all) on every playback attempt, not just the first. 0.0.26 set IsShortcut/ShortcutPath on federated items to mark their media source IsRemote, believing it was the same mechanism .strm files use - it is not. Jellyfin's ProbeProvider.FetchShortcutInfo unconditionally does File.ReadAllLines(item.Path), expecting Path to point at a real local .strm file whose contents are the target URL; since our Path already *is* that URL, the read throws DirectoryNotFoundException on every metadata refresh. Because that failure prevents MediaStreams from ever being saved, the refresh (and the failure) re-fires on every subsequent playback attempt, and clients observe this as an endless loading spinner, an HLS player left holding a torn-down transcode session (bufferAppendError), or a request that silently gives up. IsShortcut/ShortcutPath are no longer set; Path alone (an http(s) URL) already gives correct LocationType/Protocol without it, and the dynamic per-request media source (FederationMediaSourceProvider) already sets IsRemote independently and is unaffected by this bug.

0.0.28 fixed the 'Cannot deserialize unknown type' reconciliation crash reactively - only once this plugin's own background sync happened to hit it. That left a window, several seconds wide, where any other Jellyfin code path enumerating the same folder first (the web UI, a native library scan, another plugin) could still hit the same crash outside this plugin's control. The purge now runs eagerly at plugin startup, synchronously, before that window opens - so legacy items left over from 0.0.22-0.0.24 are gone before anything else gets a chance to touch them.

Fixes reconciliation still failing after upgrading to 0.0.27. Servers that had run 0.0.22-0.0.24 still had federated items stored in the database under the plugin subclasses removed in 0.0.27 (FederatedMovie, FederatedSeries, ...); Jellyfin can no longer resolve those rows back to a type and throws 'Cannot deserialize unknown type', which aborted the entire folder listing - not just the bad row - so every reconciliation of an affected library failed. Reconciliation now detects this, finds and deletes the unrecoverable rows directly by id (without needing to deserialize them), and retries. Also fixes the 0.0.27 catalog listing itself: its checksum did not match the uploaded release asset, so installing/updating via the plugin catalog failed with a checksum mismatch.

Fixes federated content not appearing at all. 0.0.22 created federated items under plugin subclasses (FederatedMovie, FederatedSeries, ...) so they could override LocationType. Jellyfin resolves an item's kind by parsing the CLR class name into its BaseItemKind enum, so those names threw - and that call sits under both DTO serialization and folder enumeration, meaning every API response containing a federated item returned a 500 and library reconciliation aborted. Items are now created as Jellyfin's own types again; the override is unnecessary because items carry a real remote URL on Path, which already resolves as Remote. Also carries the 0.0.26 streaming fix (items get the remote stream URL on Path so Jellyfin builds a real, probeable HTTP media source instead of an unplayable placeholder). Existing federated items are rebuilt once; watch progress on them is reset. The friend-request and friends-of-friends features are withdrawn for now and preserved on the archive/friend-system branch.

Add opt-in friends-of-friends federation: with the new Allow friends-of-friends setting on, this server asks its friends who their other friends are and automatically sends friend requests to anyone new it discovers (still needs their admin to accept). Off by default. Content stays scoped to what a server actually owns either way - it never re-shares content that was itself federated into it from someone else.

Federated episodes no longer show 'Missing' in the UI. They were materialized as their base Jellyfin CLR types with Path null, so LocationType resolved to Virtual - and the web client paints a 'Missing' badge on any episode with Type == Episode && LocationType == Virtual. Federated items are now created under dedicated subclasses (FederatedEpisode, FederatedMovie, ...) that report LocationType = Remote. One-time rebuild of existing federated items (watch/playback progress on them is reset once).

Fix playback for federated items lacking a configured remote UserId: PlaybackInfo now falls back to the remote's first user automatically (previously it returned null, so media sources carried no Container/MediaStreams and every client reported 'Unable to find a valid media source to play'). Adds logs to confirm stream info is resolved.

Federated seasons and episodes are visible without enabling 'Display missing episodes' (they were stamped IsVirtualItem, which Jellyfin reads as 'missing'). Seasons now carry their IndexNumber, so Jellyfin stops creating a duplicate empty season beside each real one; the duplicates it already created are removed on first sync. Media sources now carry the remote's real container and stream info, without which no client could validate playback. Rebuilds federated Series/Season/Episode items once on upgrade.
Debug logging for the 'unable to find a valid media source' playback error (seasons/episodes are now visible, so this is the next thing to fix). No database changes in this release.

The 0.0.16 fix only recreated Season/Episode items, not the Series itself - a Series never got its own PresentationUniqueKey set, so the match could still fail depending on a library setting. Series are now included in the migration too.

Fix: saving config (from any page load) silently reset the migration-complete flag, since the config page's save payload doesn't include newer fields - causing the whole episode migration to destructively rerun on every config save.

Actual fix for invisible episodes: Jellyfin's show/season pages find children by a SeriesPresentationUniqueKey match, not by parent/ancestor id. Federated episodes never had it set. One-time migration backfills it.
Fix: startup sync and the scheduled sync could run at the same time and corrupt each other mid-migration (SQLite lock errors). Syncs are now serialized, and the migration runs once more cleanly.
One-time migration: recreates existing seasons/episodes so 0.0.13's ordering fix actually applies to them (not just newly-synced ones).
Create shows/seasons/episodes in order (parent before child) so ancestry resolves correctly for browsing.
Fix: seasons were deleted right after being created, so episodes never persisted (no seasons, nothing playable).
Debug logging for the no-seasons/can't-play issue.
TV episodes now sync and play. Fixed duplicate/mismatched-watched-state shows and content looping back in from federated servers.
Actual fix for the missing-movies issue (wrong parent folder).
More debug logging for the missing-movies issue.
Debug logging for the missing-movies issue.

Fix: federated items were saved to the database as orphans, so they never appeared in any library. ILibraryManager.CreateItems does not parent the items it saves - its parent argument only feeds the ItemAdded event - and the plugin never set ParentId itself. The rows therefore matched neither the direct-children query (ParentId) nor the recursive one (AncestorIds, which Jellyfin derives from the ParentId chain at save time), leaving them invisible in the UI and invisible to the plugin's own existence check, which is why every sync re-reported the entire library as newly created. Items are now parented to their provisioned library folder. Item ids are derived deterministically from the cache key, so existing orphaned rows are adopted in place on the next sync - no manual cleanup or database reset needed. Also aligns the repository manifest guid with the plugin's actual id.

Fix: federated items never showed up. Materialized items had Path set to a federation:// URI Jellyfin doesn't recognize, so it treated them as missing/offline everywhere - hidden from browsing and from the plugin's own dedup check, which silently recreated a full duplicate set every hour. Items are now identified by a FederationKey provider id instead, with Path left null (true Virtual item). Upgrading auto-cleans any legacy federation:// duplicates on the next sync, no manual steps needed. Also triggers a background sync 5s after server start so items appear without waiting for the first scheduled task.

Fix: virtual libraries now actually provision. Jellyfin's AddVirtualFolder requires real filesystem paths, so federation:// URIs were rejected. Now uses an empty shadow folder under the plugin data dir; same-name libraries merge into one. Removal only detaches the federation location from merged libraries.
Config page rewrite: sidebar link, guided setup, working buttons, auto-detect public URL. Same-name libraries across servers merge into one. Advanced settings collapsed by default.
